stories.title: Hybrid quantum computers could finally get to grips with light and matter
stories.desc: Many of nature's most important processes depend on how particles of matter interact with light and other force-carrying particles. So far, however, it has proven difficult for conventional computers to determine how individual particles behave in these interactions.

stories.title: Quantum 'birthmarks' hold lasting traces of a system's past
stories.desc: Some classical physical systems can explore many configurations over time until their long-term behavior no longer reveals their starting conditions. The sampling of available configurations according to the appropriate statistical distribution is a property called ergodicity.

stories.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments
stories.desc: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process.
